title: Tracking the Unseen: An Occlusion-Robust Framework for Target Tracking Under Full and Long-Term Occlusion

problem.summary: Visual tracking degrades severely under full and long-term occlusion; existing trackers struggle to recover targets when they become invisible for extended periods.
statements: Occlusion, especially full and long-term occlusion, remains a major challenge for visual object tracking.
Most existing trackers assume target visibility or short-term occlusion, leading to drift or failure under prolonged invisibility.

evidence.quote: Classical trackers terminate trajectories prematurely because they have no appearance memory, and deep hybrid trackers, although more resilient, still struggle to preserve identity continuity across full and long-term occlusion events.

Two major challenges hinder
reliable performance in this regard: full occlusion, which occurs when the target is completely invisible to the detector,
and long-term occlusion, which refers to situations where a target remains partially or fully hidden for an extended
duration.

background.summary: Relates to occlusion-robust tracking and long-term tracking; identifies gap in handling full/long-term occlusion robustly.

relatedWork.name: Long-term tracking

Tracking the Unseen: An Occlusion-Robust Tracking Framework

Mohammed et al.

solution.summary: Proposes an occlusion-robust tracking framework designed to handle full and long-term occlusion through mechanisms for occlusion reasoning and reliable re-localization.
solution.approach: Occlusion-robust framework with explicit handling of full/long-term occlusion for target recovery.

evidence.quote:
The proposed framework consists of three stages:
object detection, position estimation during occlusion, and identity recovery after target reappearance.

Six Re-Identification (Re-ID) architectures were evaluated within the same tracking framework under
identical experimental conditions, with the Occlusion-Aware Mask Network (OAMN) achieving
the best overall performance and therefore selected for the final pipeline.

experiments.summary: Evaluates on occlusion-heavy/long-term tracking benchmarks, comparing to state-of-the-art trackers with metrics focused on robustness under occlusion.

evidence.quote:
On a custom military dataset designed to
simulate surveillance and battlefield-like environments with long-term occlusion, the proposed framework achieved a MOTA of 0.734 and an IDF1 of 0.729, corresponding to relative improvements of
14.2% and 5.8%, respectively, over OccluTrack.

limitations.summary: No explicit verbatim limitations prominently stated.
